args.description: An image into which to copy bands.

args.name: srcImg
args.description: An image containing bands to copy.

args.name: names
args.description: Optional list of band names to copy. If names is omitted, all bands from srcImg will be copied over.

args.name: overwrite
args.description: If true, bands from `srcImg` will override bands with the same names in `dstImg`. Otherwise the new band will be renamed with a numerical suffix (`foo` to `foo_1` unless `foo_1` exists, then `foo_2` unless it exists, etc).

Image.bandNames.description: Returns a list containing the names of the bands of an image.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to get band names.

Image.bandTypes.description: Returns a dictionary of the image's band types.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to get band types.

Image.bitsToArrayImage.description: Turns the bits of an integer into a 1-D array. The array has a length up to the highest 'on' bit in the input.

args.name: input
args.description: Input image.

Image.blend.description: Overlays one image on top of another. The images are blended together using the masks as opacity. If either of images has only 1 band, it is replicated to match the number of bands in the other image.

args.name: bottom
args.description: The bottom image.

args.name: top
args.description: The top image.

Image.cast.description: Casts some or all bands of an image to the specified types.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to cast.

args.name: bandTypes
args.description: A dictionary from band name to band types. Types can be PixelTypes or strings. The valid strings are: 'int8', 'int16', 'int32', 'int64', 'uint8', 'uint16', 'uint32', 'byte', 'short', 'int', 'long', 'float', and 'double'. If bandTypes includes bands that are not already in the input image, they will be added to the image as transparent bands. If bandOrder isn't also specified, new bands will be appended in alphabetical order.

args.name: bandOrder
args.description: A list specifying the order of the bands in the result. If specified, must match the full list of bands in the result.

Image.cat.description:
Combines a list of images into a single image which contains all bands from all of the images.

If two or more bands share a name, they are suffixed with an incrementing index.

The resulting image will have the metadata from the first input image, only.

This function will promote constant values into constant images.

args.name: images
args.description: The list of images to combine.

Image.changeProj.description: Tweaks the projection of the input image, moving each pixel from its location in srcProj to the same coordinates in dstProj.

args.name: srcProj
args.description: The original projection.

args.name: dstProj
args.description: The new projection.

Image.clamp.description: Clamps the values in all bands of an image to all lie within the specified range.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to clamp.

args.name: low
args.description: The minimum allowed value in the range.

args.name: high
args.description: The maximum allowed value in the range.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to classify. Bands are extracted from this image by name and it must contain all the bands named in the classifier's schema.

args.name: classifier
args.description: The classifier to use.

args.name: outputName
args.description: The name of the band to be added. If the classifier produces more than 1 output, this name is ignored.

Image.cluster.description: Applies a clusterer to an image. Returns a new image with a single band containing values from 0 to N, indicating the cluster each pixel is assigned to.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to cluster. Must contain all the bands in the clusterer's schema.

args.name: clusterer
args.description: The clusterer to use.

args.name: outputName
args.description: The name of the output band.

Image.connectedPixelCount.description: Generate an image where each pixel contains the number of 4- or 8-connected neighbors (including itself).

args.name: input
args.description: The input image.

args.name: maxSize
args.description: The maximum size of the neighborhood in pixels.

args.name: eightConnected
args.description: Whether to use 8-connected rather 4-connected rules.

Image.connectedComponents.description: Finds connected components with the same value of the first band of the input and labels them with a globally unique value. Connectedness is specified by the given kernel. Objects larger than maxSize are considered background, and are masked.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to label.

args.name: connectedness
args.description: Connectedness kernel.

args.name: maxSize
args.description: Maximum size of objects to be labeled.

Image.constant.description: Generates an image containing a constant value everywhere.

args.name: value
args.description: The value of the pixels in the constant image. Must be a number or an Array or a list of numbers or Arrays.

Image.convolve.description: Convolves each band of an image with the given kernel.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to convolve.

args.name: kernel
args.description: The kernel to convolve with.

Image.cumulativeCost.description:
Computes a cumulative cost map based on an image containing costs to traverse each pixel and an image containing source locations.

Each output band represents the cumulative cost over the corresponding input cost band.

args.name: cost
args.description: An image representing the cost to traverse each pixel. Masked pixels can't be traversed. When comparing pixel traversal costs, we use band-wise dictionary ordering. Ancillary cost bands are only considered when paths over primary bands are equal cost.

args.name: source
args.description: A single-band image representing the sources. A pixel value different from 0 defines a source pixel.

args.name: maxDistance
args.description: Maximum distance for computation, in meters.

args.name: geodeticDistance
args.description: If true, geodetic distance along the curved surface is used, assuming a spherical Earth of radius 6378137.0. If false, Euclidean distance in the 2D plane of the map projection is used (faster, but less accurate).

Image.date.description: Returns the acquisition time of an image as a Date object. This helper function is equivalent to `ee.Date(image.get('system:time_start'))`.

args.name: image
args.description: The image whose acquisition time to return.

Image.derivative.description:
Computes the X and Y discrete derivatives for each band in the input image, in pixel coordinates.

For each band of the input image, the output image will have two bands named with the suffixes `_x` and `_y`, containing the respective derivatives.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

Image.displace.description: Warps an image using an image of displacements.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to warp.

args.name: displacement
args.description: An image containing displacement values. The first band is interpreted as the 'X' displacement and the second as the 'Y' displacement. Each displacement pixel is a [dx,dy] vector added to the pixel location to determine the corresponding pixel location in 'image'. Displacements are interpreted as meters in the default projection of the displacement image.

args.name: mode
args.description: The interpolation mode to use. One of 'nearest_neighbor', 'bilinear', or 'bicubic'.

args.name: maxOffset
args.description: The maximum absolute offset in the displacement image. Providing this may improve processing performance.

Image.displacement.description: Determines displacements required to register an image to a reference image while  allowing local, rubber sheet deformations. Displacements are computed in the CRS  of the reference image, at a scale dictated by the lowest resolution of the following  three projections: input image projection, reference image projection, and requested  projection. The displacements are then transformed into the user-specified projection  for output.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to register.

args.name: referenceImage
args.description: The image to register to.

args.name: maxOffset
args.description: The maximum offset allowed when attempting to align the input images, in meters. Using a smaller value can reduce computation time significantly, but it must still be large enough to cover the greatest displacement within the entire image region.

args.name: projection
args.description: The projection in which to output displacement values. The default is the projection of the first band of the reference image.

args.name: patchWidth
args.description: Patch size for detecting image offsets, in meters. This should be set large enough to capture texture, as well as large enough that ignorable objects are small within the patch. Default is null. Patch size will be determined automatically if not provided.

args.name: stiffness
args.description: Enforces a stiffness constraint on the solution. Valid values are in the range [0,10]. The stiffness is used for outlier rejection when determining displacements at adjacent grid points. Higher values move the solution towards a rigid transformation. Lower values allow more distortion or warping of the image during registration.

Image.distance.description: Computes the distance to the nearest non-zero pixel in each band, using the specified distance kernel.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: kernel
args.description: The distance kernel. One of chebyshev, euclidean, or manhattan.

args.name: skipMasked
args.description: Mask output pixels if the corresponding input pixel is masked.

Image.entropy.description: Computes the windowed entropy for each band using the specified kernel centered on each input pixel. Entropy is computed as -sum(p * log2(p)), where p is the normalized probability of occurrence of the values encountered in each window.

args.name: image
args.description: The image for which to compute the entropy.

args.name: kernel
args.description: A kernel specifying the window in which to compute.

Image.fastDistanceTransform.description: Returns the distance, as determined by the specified distance metric, to the nearest non-zero valued pixel in the input. The output contains values for all pixels within the given neighborhood size, regardless of the input's mask. Note: the default distance metric returns squared distance.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: neighborhood
args.description: Neighborhood size in pixels.

args.name: units
args.description: The units of the neighborhood, currently only 'pixels' are supported.

args.name: metric
args.description: Distance metric to use: options are `squared_euclidean`, `manhattan` or `chebyshev`.

Image.directionalDistanceTransform.description:
For each zero-valued pixel in the source, get the distance to the nearest non-zero pixels in the given direction.

Returns a band of floating point distances called distance.

args.name: source
args.description: The source image.

args.name: angle
args.description: The angle, in degrees, at which to search for non-zero pixels.

args.name: maxDistance
args.description: The maximum distance, in pixels, over which to search.

args.name: labelBand
args.description: If provided, multi-band inputs are permitted and only this band is used for searching. All other bands are returned and populated with the per-band values found at the searched non-zero pixels in the label band.

Image.glcmTexture.description:
Computes texture metrics from the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix around each pixel of every band. The GLCM is a tabulation of how often different combinations of pixel brightness values (grey levels) occur in an image. It counts the number of times a pixel of value X lies next to a pixel of value Y, in a particular direction and distance. and then derives statistics from this tabulation.

This implementation computes the 14 GLCM metrics proposed by Haralick, and 4 additional metrics from Conners. Inputs are required to be integer valued.

The output consists of 18 bands per input band if directional averaging is on and 18 bands per directional pair in the kernel, if not:

  • ASM: f1, Angular Second Moment; measures the number of repeated pairs
  • CONTRAST: f2, Contrast; measures the local contrast of an image
  • CORR: f3, Correlation; measures the correlation between pairs of pixels
  • VAR: f4, Variance; measures how spread out the distribution of gray-levels is
  • IDM: f5, Inverse Difference Moment; measures the homogeneity
  • SAVG: f6, Sum Average
  • SVAR: f7, Sum Variance
  • SENT: f8, Sum Entropy
  • ENT: f9, Entropy. Measures the randomness of a gray-level distribution
  • DVAR: f10, Difference variance
  • DENT: f11, Difference entropy
  • IMCORR1: f12, Information Measure of Corr. 1
  • IMCORR2: f13, Information Measure of Corr. 2
  • MAXCORR: f14, Max Corr. Coefficient. (not computed)
  • DISS: Dissimilarity
  • INERTIA: Inertia
  • SHADE: Cluster Shade
  • PROM: Cluster prominence
More information can be found in the two papers: Haralick et. al, 'Textural Features for Image Classification', https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1973.4309314 and Conners, et al, 'Segmentation of a high-resolution urban scene using texture operators', https://doi.org/10.1016/0734-189X(84)90197-X.

args.name: image
args.description: The image for which to compute texture metrics.

args.name: size
args.description: The size of the neighborhood to include in each GLCM. For example, the size of 1 corresponds to a 3x3 square, the size of 2 corresponds to a 5x5 square, the size of 3 corresponds to a 7x7 square, etc.

args.name: kernel
args.description: A kernel specifying the x and y offsets over which to compute the GLCMs. A GLCM is computed for each pixel in the kernel that is non-zero, except the center pixel and as long as a GLCM hasn't already been computed for the same direction and distance. For example, if either or both of the east and west pixels are set, only 1 (horizontal) GLCM is computed. Kernels are scanned from left to right and top to bottom. The default is a 3x3 square, resulting in 4 GLCMs with the offsets (-1, -1), (0, -1), (1, -1) and (-1, 0).

args.name: average
args.description: If true, the directional bands for each metric are averaged.

Image.gradient.description: Calculates the x and y gradient.

args.name: input
args.description: The input image.

Image.hsvToRgb.description: Transforms the image from the HSV color space to the RGB color space. Expects a 3-band image in the range [0, 1], and produces 3 bands: red, green and blue with values in the range [0, 1].

args.name: image
args.description: The image to transform.

Image.interpolate.description:
Interpolates each point in the first band of the input image into the piecewise-linear function specified by the x and y arrays. The x values must be strictly increasing. If an input point is less than the first or greater than the last x value, then the output is specified by the "behavior" argument:
  1. "extrapolate" specifies the output value is extrapolated from the two nearest points.
  2. "clamp" specifies the output value is taken from the nearest point.
  3. "input" specifies the output value is copied from the input.
  4. "mask" specifies the output value is masked.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to which the interpolation is applied.

args.name: x
args.description: The x axis (input) values in the piecewise function.

args.name: y
args.description: The y axis (output) values in the piecewise function.

args.name: behavior
args.description: The behavior for points that are outside of the range of the supplied function. Options are: 'extrapolate', 'clamp', 'mask', or 'input'.

Image.linkCollection.description:
Links the source image to a matching image from an image collection.

Any specified bands or metadata will be added to the source image from the image found in the collection, and if the bands or metadata are already present they will be overwritten. If a matching image is not found, any new or updated bands will be fully masked and any new or updated metadata will be null. The output footprint will be the same as the source image footprint.

A match is determined if the source image and an image in the collection have a specific equivalent metadata property. If more than one collection image would match, the collection image selected is arbitrary. By default, images are matched on their 'system:index' metadata property.

This linking function is a convenience method for adding bands to a target image based on a specified shared metadata property and is intended to support linking collections that apply different processing/product generation to the same source imagery. For more expressive linking known as 'joining', see https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/guides/joins_intro.

args.name: input
args.description: The source image a matching image in the collection will be linked to.

args.name: imageCollection
args.description: The image collection searched to extract an image matching the source.

args.name: linkedBands
args.description: A band name or list of band names to add or update from the matching image.

args.name: linkedProperties
args.description: A metadata property or list of properties to add or update from the matching image.

args.name: matchPropertyName
args.description: The metadata property name to use as a match criteria.

Image.load.description: Returns the image given its ID.

args.name: id
args.description: The asset ID of the image.

args.name: version
args.description: The version of the asset. -1 signifies the latest version.

Image.loadGeoTIFF.description: Loads a GeoTIFF as an Image.

args.name: uri
args.description: The Cloud Storage URI of the GeoTIFF to load. The bucket metadata must be accessible (requires the `storage.buckets.get` permission which is provided by the role "Storage Legacy Bucket Reader" among others, see https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam-roles) and the bucket must be located in the US multi-region, a dual-region including US-CENTRAL1, or the US-CENTRAL1 region.

Image.loadMosaic.description: Loads a mosaic metadata file as an Image.

args.name: uri
args.description: The Cloud Storage URI of the mosaic metadata file to load.

Image.loadZarrV2Array.description: Loads a Zarr v2 array as an Image. The array attributes (.zattrs) must contain the field '_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS', which is a list of the names of each dimension (e.g., ['time', 'y', 'x']). There must be at least two dimensions, with the final two representing Y and X respectively (e.g., ['lat', 'lon']). The supported compression codecs are 'blosc', 'gzip', 'lz4', 'zlib', and 'zstd'. The supported blosc meta-compression codecs are 'lz4', lz4hc', 'zlib', and 'zstd' ('blosclz' is not supported).

args.name: uri
args.description: The Cloud Storage URI of the .zarray file to load. A .zmetadata file must be present in the parent directory of the array's directory (e.g., for 'gs://b/o/.zarray', 'gs://b/.zmetadata' must be present). The bucket metadata must be accessible (requires the `storage.buckets.get` permission which is provided by the role "Storage Legacy Bucket Reader" among others, see https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam-roles) and the bucket must be located in the US multi-region, a dual-region including US-CENTRAL1, or the US-CENTRAL1 region.

args.name: proj
args.description: The projection of the array.

args.name: starts
args.description: The indices (inclusive) at which to start taking slices along each non-spatial dimension. If null, slices will start at index 0 for all non-spatial dimensions. If specified, this list must have a length equal to the number of non-spatial dimensions (total dimensions - 2). An individual element within the list may be null, which defaults to 0 for that dimension. Negative indices are counted from the end of the dimension (e.g., -1 is the last element).

args.name: ends
args.description: The indices (exclusive) at which to stop taking slices along each non-spatial dimension. If null, slices will extend to the end of each corresponding non-spatial dimension (i.e., defaults to the length of the dimension). If specified, this list must have a length equal to the number of non-spatial dimensions (total dimensions - 2). An individual element within the list may be null, which also defaults to the length of that dimension. Negative indices are counted from the end of the dimension (e.g., -1 is the last element).

Image.mask.description:
Gets or sets an image's mask. The output image retains the metadata and footprint of the input image. Pixels where the mask changes from zero to another value will be filled with zeros, or the values closest to zero within the range of the pixel type.

Note: the version that sets a mask will be deprecated. To set a mask from an image on previously unmasked pixels, use Image.updateMask. To unmask previously masked pixels, use Image.unmask.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: mask
args.description: The mask image. If specified, the input image is copied to the output but given the mask by the values of this image. If this is a single band, it is used for all bands in the input image. If not specified, returns an image created from the mask of the input image, scaled to the range [0:1] (invalid = 0, valid = 1.0).

Image.medialAxis.description:
Computes the discrete medial axis of the zero valued pixels of the first band of the input. Outputs 4 bands:

  1. medial - the medial axis points, scaled by the distance.
  2. coverage - the number of points supporting each medial axis point.
  3. xlabel - the horizontal distance to the power point for each pixel.
  4. ylabel - the vertical distance to the power point for each pixel.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: neighborhood
args.description: Neighborhood size in pixels.

args.name: units
args.description: The units of the neighborhood, currently only 'pixels' are supported.

Image.metadata.description: Generates a constant image of type double from a metadata property.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to get the metadata

args.name: property
args.description: The property from which to take the value.

args.name: name
args.description: The name for the output band. If unspecified, it will be the same as the property name.

Image.neighborhoodToBands.description:
Turns the neighborhood of a pixel into a set of bands. The neighborhood is specified using a Kernel and only non-zero-weight kernel values are used. The weights of the kernel is otherwise ignored.

Each input band produces x * y output bands. Each output band is named 'input_x_y' where x and y indicate the pixel's location in the kernel. For example, a 3x3 kernel operating on a 2-band image produces 18 output bands.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to get pixels from.

args.name: kernel
args.description: The kernel specifying the neighborhood. Zero-weight values are ignored.

Image.neighborhoodToArray.description: Turns the neighborhood of each pixel in a scalar image into a 2D array. Axes 0 and 1 of the output array correspond to Y and X axes of the image, respectively. The output image will have as many bands as the input; each output band has the same mask as the corresponding input band. The footprint and metadata of the input image are preserved.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to get pixels from; must be scalar-valued.

args.name: kernel
args.description: The kernel specifying the shape of the neighborhood. Only fixed, square and rectangle kernels are supported. Weights are ignored; only the shape of the kernel is used.

args.name: defaultValue
args.description: The value to use in the output arrays to replace the invalid (masked) pixels of the input. If the band type is integral, the fractional part of this value is discarded; in all cases, the value is clamped to the value range of the band.

Image.normalizedDifference.description:
Computes the normalized difference between two bands. If the bands to use are not specified, uses the first two bands. The normalized difference is computed as (first − second) / (first + second).

Note that the returned image band name is 'nd', the input image properties are not retained in the output image, and a negative pixel value in either input band will cause the output pixel to be masked. To avoid masking negative input values, use `ee.Image.expression()` to compute normalized difference.

args.name: input
args.description: The input image.

args.name: bandNames
args.description: A list of names specifying the bands to use. If not specified, the first and second bands are used.

Image.paint.description:
Paints the geometries of a collection onto an image, using the given 'color' value to replace each band's values where any geometry covers the image (or, if a line width is specified, where the perimeters do).

This algorithm is most suitable for converting categorical data from feature properties to pixels in an image; if you wish to visualize a collection, consider using FeatureCollection.style instead, which supports RGB colors whereas this algorithm is strictly 'monochrome' (using single numeric values).

args.name: image
args.description: The image on which the collection is painted.

args.name: featureCollection
args.description: The collection painted onto the image.

args.name: color
args.description: The pixel value to paint into every band of the input image, either as a number which will be used for all features, or the name of a numeric property to take from each feature in the collection.

args.name: width
args.description: Line width, either as a number which will be the line width for all geometries, or the name of a numeric property to take from each feature in the collection. If unspecified, the geometries will be filled instead of outlined.

Image.parseExpression.description:
Generates an algorithm from an arithmetic expression on images.

By default the generated algorithm takes one argument to denote the 'default' image. Other variables in the expression are interpreted as image arguments that will be passed to the returned algorithm. The bands of each image can be accessed as image.band_name or image[0]. The bands of the default image are available using the built-in function b(), as b(0) or b('band_name'). Both b() and image[] allow multiple arguments, to specify multiple bands, such as b(1, 'name', 3). Calling b() with no arguments returns all bands of the image. If the result of an expression is a single band, it can be assigned a name using the '=' operator (e.g., x = a + b).

args.name: expression
args.description: The expression to parse.

args.name: argName
args.description: The name of the default image argument.

args.name: vars
args.description: The parameters the resulting algorithm should have, which must be a superset of the free variables in the expression, including the default image argument if it is used.

args.name: mapFreeVarsToDefaultImageBands
args.description: If true, the resulting algorithm will map free variables to the default image's bands instead of throwing an error.

Image.pixelArea.description: Generate an image in which the value of each pixel is the area of that pixel in square meters. The returned image has a single band called "area."

Image.pixelCoordinates.description: Creates a two-band image containing the x and y coordinates of each pixel in the given projection.

args.name: projection
args.description: The projection in which to provide pixels.

Image.pixelLonLat.description: Creates an image with two bands named 'longitude' and 'latitude', containing the longitude and latitude at each pixel, in degrees.

Image.polynomial.description: Compute a polynomial at each pixel using the given coefficients.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: coefficients
args.description: The polynomial coefficients in increasing order of degree starting with the constant term.

Image.projection.description: Returns the default projection of an Image. Throws an error if the bands of the image don't all have the same projection.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to get the projection.

Image.random.description: Generates a random number at each pixel location. When using the 'uniform' distribution, outputs are in the range of [0, 1). Using the 'normal' distribution, the outputs have μ=0, σ=1, but no explicit limits.

args.name: seed
args.description: Seed for the random number generator.

args.name: distribution
args.description: The distribution type of random numbers to produce. One of 'uniform' or 'normal'.

Image.randomVisualizer.description: Creates a visualization image by assigning a random color to each unique value of the pixels of the first band. The first three bands of the output image will contain 8-bit R, G and B values, followed by all bands of the input image.

args.name: image
args.description: Image with at least one band.

Image.reduceNeighborhood.description:
Applies the given reducer to the neighborhood around each pixel, as determined by the given kernel. If the reducer has a single input, it will be applied separately to each band of the collection; otherwise it must have the same number of inputs as the input image has bands.

The reducer output names determine the names of the output bands:

  • Reducers with multiple inputs will use the output names directly.
  • Reducers with a single input will prefix the output name with the input band name (e.g., '10_mean', '20_mean').

Reducers with weighted inputs can have the input weight based on the input mask, the kernel value, or the smaller of those two.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply to pixels within the neighborhood.

args.name: kernel
args.description: The kernel defining the neighborhood.

args.name: inputWeight
args.description: One of 'mask', 'kernel', or 'min'.

args.name: skipMasked
args.description: Mask output pixels if the corresponding input pixel is masked.

args.name: optimization
args.description: Optimization strategy. Options are 'boxcar' and 'window'. The 'boxcar' method is a fast method for computing count, sum or mean. It requires a homogeneous kernel, a single-input reducer and either MASK, KERNEL or no weighting. The 'window' method uses a running window, and has the same requirements as 'boxcar', but can use any single input reducer. Both methods require considerable additional memory.

Image.reduce.description:
Applies a reducer to all of the bands of an image.

The reducer must have a single input and will be called at each pixel to reduce the stack of band values.

The output image will have one band for each reducer output.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to reduce.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply to the given image.

Image.reduceRegion.description:
Apply a reducer to all the pixels in a specific region.

Either the reducer must have the same number of inputs as the input image has bands, or it must have a single input and will be repeated for each band.

Returns a dictionary of the reducer's outputs.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to reduce.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply.

args.name: geometry
args.description: The region over which to reduce data. Defaults to the footprint of the image's first band.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to work in.

args.name: crs
args.description: The projection to work in. If unspecified, the projection of the image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The list of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of the 3x2 transform matrix. This option is mutually exclusive with 'scale', and replaces any transform already set on the projection.

args.name: bestEffort
args.description: If the polygon would contain too many pixels at the given scale, compute and use a larger scale which would allow the operation to succeed.

args.name: maxPixels
args.description: The maximum number of pixels to reduce.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor between 0.1 and 16 used to adjust aggregation tile size; setting a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) uses smaller tiles and may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

Image.reduceRegions.description:
Apply a reducer over the area of each feature in the given collection.

The reducer must have the same number of inputs as the input image has bands.

Returns the input features, each augmented with the corresponding reducer outputs.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to reduce.

args.name: collection
args.description: The features to reduce over.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to work in.

args.name: crs
args.description: The projection to work in. If unspecified, the projection of the image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The list of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of the 3x2 transform matrix. This option is mutually exclusive with 'scale', and will replace any transform already set on the projection.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to reduce aggregation tile size; using a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

args.name: maxPixelsPerRegion
args.description: The maximum number of pixels to reduce per region.

Image.reduceResolution.description:
Enables reprojection using the given reducer to combine all input pixels corresponding to each output pixel. If the reducer has a single input, it will be applied separately to each band of the collection; otherwise it must have the same number of inputs as the input image has bands.
The reducer output names determine the names of the output bands: reducers with multiple inputs will use the output names directly, reducers with a single input and single output will preserve the input band names, and reducers with a single input and multiple outputs will prefix the output name with the input band name (e.g., '10_mean', '10_stdDev', '20_mean', '20_stdDev').
Reducer input weights will be the product of the input mask and the fraction of the output pixel covered by the input pixel.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply to be used for combining pixels.

args.name: bestEffort
args.description: If using the input at its default resolution would require too many pixels, start with already-reduced input pixels from a pyramid level that allows the operation to succeed.

args.name: maxPixels
args.description: The maximum number of input pixels to combine for each output pixel. Setting this too large will cause out-of-memory problems.

Image.reduceToVectors.description:
Convert an image to a feature collection by reducing homogeneous regions.

Given an image containing a band of labeled segments and zero or more additional bands, runs a reducer over the pixels in each segment producing a feature per segment.

Either the reducer must have one fewer inputs than the image has bands, or it must have a single input and will be repeated for each band.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image. The first band is expected to be an integer type; adjacent pixels will be in the same segment if they have the same value in this band.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply. Its inputs will be taken from the image's bands after dropping the first band. Defaults to Reducer.countEvery().

args.name: geometry
args.description: The region over which to reduce data. Defaults to the footprint of the image's first band.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to work in.

args.name: geometryType
args.description: How to choose the geometry of each generated feature; one of 'polygon' (a polygon enclosing the pixels in the segment), 'bb' (a rectangle bounding the pixels), or 'centroid' (the centroid of the pixels).

args.name: eightConnected
args.description: If true, diagonally-connected pixels are considered adjacent; otherwise only pixels that share an edge are.

args.name: labelProperty
args.description: If non-null, the value of the first band will be saved as the specified property of each feature.

args.name: crs
args.description: The projection to work in. If unspecified, the projection of the image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The list of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of the 3x2 transform matrix. This option is mutually exclusive with 'scale', and replaces any transform already set on the projection.

args.name: bestEffort
args.description: If the polygon would contain too many pixels at the given scale, compute and use a larger scale which would allow the operation to succeed.

args.name: maxPixels
args.description: The maximum number of pixels to reduce.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to reduce aggregation tile size; using a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

args.name: geometryInNativeProjection
args.description: Create geometries in the pixel projection, rather than EPSG:4326.

Image.reduceToVectorsStreaming.description:
Convert an image to a feature collection by reducing homogeneous regions. Given an image containing a band of labeled segments and zero or more additional bands, runs a reducer over the pixels in each segment producing a feature per segment.

Either the reducer must have one fewer inputs than the image has bands, or it must have a single input and will be repeated for each band.

args.name: geometry

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to work in.

args.name: geometryType
args.description: How to choose the geometry of each generated feature; one of 'polygon' (a polygon enclosing the pixels in the segment), 'bb' (a rectangle bounding the pixels), or 'centroid' (the centroid of the pixels).

args.name: eightConnected

args.name: crsTransform
