Image.regexpRename.description: Renames the bands of an image by applying a regular expression replacement to the current band names. Any bands not matched by the regex will be copied over without renaming.

args.name: input
args.description: The image containing the bands to rename.

args.name: regex
args.description: A regular expression to match in each band name.

args.name: replacement
args.description: The text with which to replace each match. Supports $n syntax for captured values.

args.name: all
args.description: If true, all matches in a given string will be replaced. Otherwise, only the first match in each string will be replaced.

Image.rename.description: Renames the bands of an image.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to select bands from.

args.name: names
args.description: New names for the image's bands. Must exactly match the number of bands in input.

Image.remap.description: Maps from input values to output values, represented by two parallel lists. Any input values not included in the input list are either set to defaultValue if it is given or masked if it isn't. Note that inputs containing floating point values might sometimes fail to match due to floating point precision errors.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to which the remapping is applied.

args.name: from
args.description: The source values (numbers or ee.Array). All values in this list will be mapped to the corresponding value in 'to'.

args.name: to
args.description: The destination values (numbers or ee.Array). These are used to replace the corresponding values in 'from'. Must have the same number of values as 'from'.

args.name: defaultValue
args.description: The default value to replace values that weren't matched by a value in 'from'. If not specified, unmatched values are masked out.

args.name: bandName
args.description: The name of the band to remap. If not specified, the first band in the image is used.

Image.reproject.description: Force an image to be computed in a given projection and resolution.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to reproject.

args.name: crs
args.description: The CRS to project the image to.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The list of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of the 3x2 transform matrix. This option is mutually exclusive with the scale option, and replaces any transform already on the projection.

args.name: scale
args.description: If scale is specified, then the projection is scaled by dividing the specified scale value by the nominal size of a meter in the specified projection. If scale is not specified, then the scale of the given projection will be used.

Image.rgbToHsv.description: Transforms the image from the RGB color space to the HSV color space. Expects a 3-band image in the range [0, 1], and produces 3 bands: hue, saturation and value with values in the range [0, 1].

args.name: image
args.description: The image to transform.

Image.resample.description:
An algorithm that returns an image identical to its argument, but which uses bilinear or bicubic interpolation (rather than the default nearest-neighbor) to compute pixels in projections other than its native projection or other levels of the same image pyramid.

This relies on the input image's default projection being meaningful, and so cannot be used on composites, for example. (Instead, you should resample the images that are used to create the composite.)

args.name: image
args.description: The Image to resample.

args.name: mode
args.description: The interpolation mode to use. One of 'bilinear' or 'bicubic'.

Image.rsedTransform.description: Reverse Squared Euclidean Distance (RSED) computes the 2D maximal height surface created by placing an inverted parabola over each non-zero pixel of the input image, where the pixel's value is the height of the parabola. Viewed as a binary image (zero/not-zero) this is equivalent to buffering each non-zero input pixel by the square root of its value, in pixels.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: neighborhood
args.description: Neighborhood size in pixels.

args.name: units
args.description: The units of the neighborhood, currently only 'pixels' are supported.

Image.sample.description: Samples the pixels of an image, returning them as a FeatureCollection. Each feature will have 1 property per band in the input image. Note that the default behavior is to drop features that intersect masked pixels, which result in null-valued properties (see dropNulls argument).

args.name: image
args.description: The image to sample.

args.name: region
args.description: The region to sample from. If unspecified, uses the image's whole footprint.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to sample in.

args.name: projection
args.description: The projection in which to sample. If unspecified, the projection of the image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: factor
args.description: A subsampling factor, within (0, 1]. If specified, 'numPixels' must not be specified. Defaults to no subsampling.

args.name: numPixels
args.description: The approximate number of pixels to sample. If specified, 'factor' must not be specified.

args.name: seed
args.description: A randomization seed to use for subsampling.

args.name: dropNulls
args.description: Post filter the result to drop features that have null-valued properties.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to reduce aggregation tile size; using a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

args.name: geometries
args.description: If true, adds the center of the sampled pixel as the geometry property of the output feature. Otherwise, geometries will be omitted (saving memory).

Image.sampleRegions.description:
Converts each pixel of an image (at a given scale) that intersects one or more regions to a Feature, returning them as a FeatureCollection. Each output feature will have one property per band of the input image, as well as any specified properties copied from the input feature.

Note that geometries will be snapped to pixel centers.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to sample.

args.name: collection
args.description: The regions to sample over.

args.name: properties
args.description: The list of properties to copy from each input feature. Defaults to all non-system properties.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to sample in. If unspecified, the scale of the image's first band is used.

args.name: projection
args.description: The projection in which to sample. If unspecified, the projection of the image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to reduce aggregation tile size; using a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

args.name: geometries
args.description: If true, the results will include a point geometry per sampled pixel. Otherwise, geometries will be omitted (saving memory).

Image.sampleRectangle.description: Extracts a rectangular region of pixels from an image into a ND array per band. The arrays are returned in a feature retaining the same properties as the image and a geometry the same as that used to sample the image (or the image footprint if unspecified). Each band is sampled in its input projection, and if no geometry is specified, sampled using its footprint. For scalar bands, the output array is 2D. For array bands the output array is (2+N)D where N is the number of dimensions in the original band. If sampling array bands, all arrays must have the same number of elements. If a band's sampled region is entirely masked and a default array value is specified, the default array value is used in-lieu of sampling the image.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to sample.

args.name: region
args.description: The region whose projected bounding box is used to sample the image. Defaults to the footprint in each band.

args.name: properties
args.description: The properties to copy over from the sampled image. Defaults to all non-system properties.

args.name: defaultValue
args.description: A default value used when a sampled pixel is masked or outside a band's footprint.

args.name: defaultArrayValue
args.description: A default value used when a sampled array pixel is masked or outside a band's footprint.

Image.select.description: Selects bands from an image by name, RE2-compatible regex, or index and optionally renames them.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to select bands from.

args.name: bandSelectors
args.description: A list of names, regexes, or numeric indices specifying the bands to select.

args.name: newNames
args.description: Optional new names for the output bands. Must match the number of bands selected.

Image.selfMask.description: Updates an image's mask at all positions where the existing mask is not zero using the value of the image as the new mask value. The output image retains the metadata and footprint of the input image.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to mask with itself.

Image.setDefaultProjection.description: Set a default projection to be applied to this image. The projection's resolution may be overridden by later operations.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to reproject.

args.name: crs
args.description: The CRS to project the image to.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The list of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of the 3x2 transform matrix. This option is mutually exclusive with the scale option, and replaces any transform already on the projection.

args.name: scale
args.description: If scale is specified, then the projection is scaled by dividing the specified scale value by the nominal size of a meter in the specified projection. If scale is not specified, then the scale of the given projection will be used.

Image.sldStyle.description:
Styles a raster input with the provided OGC SLD styling.

Points of note:

  • OGC SLD 1.0 and OGC SE 1.1 are supported.
  • The XML document passed in can be complete, or just the SldRasterSymbolizer element and down.
  • Exactly one SldRasterSymbolizer is required.
  • Bands may be selected by their proper Earth Engine names or using numeric identifiers ("1", "2", ...). Proper Earth Engine names are tried first.
  • The Histogram and Normalize contrast stretch mechanisms are supported.
  • The type="values", type="intervals" and type="ramp" attributes for ColorMap element in SLD 1.0 (GeoServer extensions) are supported.
  • Opacity is only taken into account when it is 0.0 (transparent). Non-zero opacity values are treated as completely opaque.
  • The OverlapBehavior definition is currently ignored.
  • The ShadedRelief mechanism is not currently supported.
  • The ImageOutline mechanism is not currently supported.
  • The Geometry element is ignored.
The output image will have histogram_bandname metadata if histogram equalization or normalization is requested.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to rendering using the SLD.

args.name: sldXml
args.description: The OGC SLD 1.0 or 1.1 document (or fragment).

Image.slice.description: Selects a contiguous group of bands from an image by position.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to select bands.

args.name: start
args.description: Where to start the selection. Negative numbers select from the end, counting backwards.

args.name: end
args.description: Where to end the selection. If omitted, selects all bands from the start position to the end.

Image.stratifiedSample.description: Extracts a stratified random sample of points from an image. Extracts the specified  number of samples for each distinct value discovered within the 'classBand'. Returns a  FeatureCollection of 1 Feature per extracted point, with each feature having 1  property per band in the input image. If there are less than the specified number  of samples available for a given class value, then all of the points for  that class will be included. Requires that the classBand contain integer values.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to sample.

args.name: numPoints
args.description: The default number of points to sample in each class. Can be overridden for specific classes using the 'classValues' and 'classPoints' properties.

args.name: classBand
args.description: The name of the band containing the classes to use for stratification. If unspecified, the first band of the input image is used.

args.name: region
args.description: The region to sample from. If unspecified, the input image's whole footprint is used.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to sample in. Defaults to the scale of the first band of the input image.

args.name: projection
args.description: The projection in which to sample. If unspecified, the projection of the input image's first band is used. If specified in addition to scale, rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: seed
args.description: A randomization seed to use for subsampling.

args.name: classValues
args.description: A list of class values for which to override the numPoints parameter. Must be the same size as classPoints or null.

args.name: classPoints
args.description: A list of the per-class maximum number of pixels to sample for each class in the classValues list. Must be the same size as classValues or null.

args.name: dropNulls
args.description: Skip pixels in which any band is masked.

args.name: tileScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to reduce aggregation tile size; using a larger tileScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

args.name: geometries
args.description: If true, the results will include a geometry per sampled pixel. Otherwise, geometries will be omitted (saving memory).

Image.register.description: Registers an image to a reference image while allowing local, rubber sheet deformations. Displacements are computed in the CRS of the reference image, at a scale dictated by the lowest resolution of the following three projections: input image projection, reference image projection, and requested projection. The displacements then applied to the input image to register it with the reference.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to register.

args.name: referenceImage
args.description: The image to register to.

args.name: maxOffset
args.description: The maximum offset allowed when attempting to align the input images, in meters. Using a smaller value can reduce computation time significantly, but it must still be large enough to cover the greatest displacement within the entire image region.

args.name: patchWidth
args.description: Patch size for detecting image offsets, in meters. This should be set large enough to capture texture, as well as large enough that ignorable objects are small within the patch. Default is null. Patch size will be determined automatically if not provided.

args.name: stiffness
args.description: Enforces a stiffness constraint on the solution. Valid values are in the range [0,10]. The stiffness is used for outlier rejection when determining displacements at adjacent grid points. Higher values move the solution towards a rigid transformation. Lower values allow more distortion or warping of the image during registration.

Image.retile.description:
Change the size of tiles in which the input image is calculated.

When pixels of this image are needed, they are computed in tiles of at most the specified size. This allows a memory-intensive image computation, such as one involving large array bands, to be broken up into smaller pieces that will fit into memory where larger ones would not.

Currently, if the image is used in a reduce operation, the tileScale parameter should be used instead of retile(). retile() is supported by Export.image but its behavior in other export tasks is not guaranteed.

args.name: image
args.description: Input image. The result will have the same bands and properties.

args.name: size
args.description: Edge length in pixels of the tile grid to use; must be between 1 and 32768.

args.name: x
args.description: The amount to translate the image in the x direction.

args.name: y
args.description: The amount to translate the image in the y direction.

args.name: units
args.description: The units for x and y; 'meters' or 'pixels'.

args.name: proj
args.description: The projection in which to translate the image; defaults to the projection of the first band.

Image.unitScale.description: Scales the input so that the range of input values [low, high] becomes [0, 1]. Values outside the range are NOT clamped. This algorithm always produces floating point pixels.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to scale.

args.name: low
args.description: The value mapped to 0.

args.name: high
args.description: The value mapped to 1.

Image.unmask.description:
Replaces mask and value of the input image with the mask and value of another image at all positions where the input mask is zero.

The output image retains the metadata of the input image. By default, the output image also retains the footprint of the input, but setting sameFootprint to false allows to extend the footprint.

args.name: input
args.description: Input image.

args.name: value
args.description: New value and mask for the masked pixels of the input image. If not specified, defaults to constant zero image which is valid everywhere.

args.name: sameFootprint
args.description: If true (or unspecified), the output retains the footprint of the input image. If false, the footprint of the output is the union of the input footprint with the footprint of the value image.

Image.unmix.description: Unmix each pixel with the given endmembers, by computing the pseudo-inverse and multiplying it through each pixel. Returns an image of doubles with the same number of bands as endmembers.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: endmembers
args.description: The endmembers to unmix with.

args.name: sumToOne
args.description: Constrain the outputs to sum to one.

args.name: nonNegative
args.description: Constrain the outputs to be non-negative.

Image.updateMask.description: Updates an image's mask at all positions where the existing mask is not zero. The output image retains the metadata and footprint of the input image.

args.name: image
args.description: Input image.

args.name: mask
args.description: New mask for the image, as a floating-point value in the range [0, 1] (invalid = 0, valid = 1). If this image has a single band, it is used for all bands in the input image; otherwise, must have the same number of bands as the input image.

Image.visualize.description: Produces an RGB or grayscale visualization of an image. Each of the gain, bias, min, max and gamma arguments can take either a single value, which will be applied to all bands, or a list of values the same length as bands.

args.name: image
args.description: The image to visualize.

args.name: bands
args.description: A list of the bands to visualize. If empty, the first 3 are used.

args.name: gain
args.description: The visualization gain(s) to use.

args.name: bias
args.description: The visualization bias(es) to use.

args.name: min
args.description: The value(s) to map to RGB8 value 0.

args.name: max
args.description: The value(s) to map to RGB8 value 255.

args.name: gamma
args.description: The gamma correction factor(s) to use.

args.name: opacity
args.description: The opacity scaling factor to use.

args.name: palette
args.description: The color palette to use. List of CSS color identifiers or hexadecimal color strings (e.g., ['red', '00FF00', 'blueviolet']).

args.name: forceRgbOutput
args.description: Whether to produce RGB output even for single-band inputs.

Image.where.description:
Performs conditional replacement of values.

For each pixel in each band of 'input', if the corresponding pixel in 'test' is nonzero, output the corresponding pixel in value, otherwise output the input pixel.

If at a given pixel, either test or value is masked, the input value is used. If the input is masked, nothing is done.

The output bands have the same names as the input bands. The output type of each band is the larger of the input and value types. The output image retains the metadata and footprint of the input image.

args.name: input
args.description: The input image.

args.name: test
args.description: The test image. The pixels of this image determines which of the input pixels is returned. If this is a single band, it is used for all bands in the input image. This may not be an array image.

args.name: value
args.description: The output value to use where test is not zero. If this is a single band, it is used for all bands in the input image.

Image.zeroCrossing.description: Finds zero-crossings on each band of an image.

args.name: image
args.description: The image from which to compute zero crossings.

Image.hersFeature.description: Computes the Histogram Error Ring Statistic (HERS) for each pixel in each band matching the keys in the descriptor. Only the bands for which HERS could be computed are returned.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: reference
args.description: The reference descriptor computed with ee.Feature.hersDescriptor(...).

args.name: peakWidthScale
args.description: The HERS peak width scale.

Image.hersImage.description: Computes the Histogram Error Ring Statistic (HERS) for each pair of pixels in each band present in both images. Only the bands for which HERS could be computed are returned.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: image2
args.description: The image to compare.

args.name: radius
args.description: The radius of the window.

args.name: buckets
args.description: The number of HERS buckets.

args.name: peakWidthScale
args.description: The HERS peak width scale.

Image.clip.description: Clips an image to a Geometry or Feature (use clipToCollection to clip an image to a FeatureCollection). The output bands correspond exactly to the input bands, except data not covered by the geometry is masked. The output image retains the metadata of the input image.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to clip.

args.name: geometry
args.description: The Geometry or Feature to clip to.

Image.clipToBoundsAndScale.description:
Clips an image to the bounds of a Geometry, and scales the clipped image to a particular size or scale.
Caution: providing a large or complex collection as the `geometry` argument can result in poor performance. Collating the geometry of collections does not scale well; use the smallest collection (or geometry) that is required to achieve the desired outcome.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to clip and scale.

args.name: geometry
args.description: The Geometry to clip the image to. The image will be clipped to the bounding box, in the image's projection, of this geometry.

args.name: width
args.description: The width to scale the image to, in pixels. Must be provided along with "height". Exclusive with "maxDimension" and "scale".

args.name: height
args.description: The height to scale the image to, in pixels. Must be provided along with "width". Exclusive with "maxDimension" and "scale".

args.name: maxDimension
args.description: The maximum dimension to scale the image to, in pixels. Exclusive with "width", "height" and "scale".

args.name: scale
args.description: If scale is specified, then the projection is scaled by dividing the specified scale value by the nominal size of a meter in the image's projection. Exclusive with "width", "height", and "maxDimension".

Image.clipToCollection.description: Clips an image to a FeatureCollection. The output bands correspond exactly the input bands, except data not covered by the geometry of at least one feature from the collection is masked. The output image retains the metadata of the input image.

args.name: input
args.description: The image to clip.

args.name: collection
args.description: The FeatureCollection to clip to.

Image.Segmentation.SNIC.description:
Superpixel clustering based on SNIC (Simple Non-Iterative Clustering). Outputs a band of cluster IDs and the per-cluster averages for each of the input bands. If the 'seeds' image isn't provided as input, the output will include a 'seeds' band containing the generated seed locations.

See: Achanta, Radhakrishna and Susstrunk, Sabine, 'Superpixels and Polygons using Simple Non-Iterative Clustering', CVPR, 2017.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image for clustering.

args.name: size
args.description: The superpixel seed location spacing, in pixels. If 'seeds' image is provided, no grid is produced.

args.name: compactness
args.description: Compactness factor. Larger values cause clusters to be more compact (square). Setting this to 0 disables spatial distance weighting.

args.name: connectivity
args.description: Connectivity. Either 4 or 8.

args.name: neighborhoodSize
args.description: Tile neighborhood size (to avoid tile boundary artifacts). Defaults to 2 * size.

args.name: seeds
args.description: If provided, any non-zero valued pixels are used as seed locations. Pixels that touch (as specified by 'connectivity') are considered to belong to the same cluster.

args.name: size
args.description: The superpixel seed location spacing, in pixels.

args.name: gridType
args.description: Type of grid. One of 'square' or 'hex'.

Image.spectralErosion.description:
Computes the spectral/spatial erosion of an image by computing the spectral distance of each pixel under a structuring kernel from the centroid of all pixels under the kernel and taking the closest result.

See 'Spatial/spectral endmember extraction by multidimensional morphological operations.' IEEE transactions on geoscience and remote sensing 40.9 (2002): 2025-2041.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: metric
args.description: The spectral distance metric to use. One of 'sam' (spectral angle mapper), 'sid' (spectral information divergence), 'sed' (squared Euclidean distance), or 'emd' (earth movers distance).

args.name: kernel
args.description: Connectedness kernel. Defaults to a square of radius 1 (8-way connected).

args.name: useCentroid
args.description: If true, distances are computed from the mean of all pixels under the kernel instead of the kernel's center pixel.

Image.spectralGradient.description:
Computes the spectral gradient over all bands of an image (or the first band if the image is Array typed) by computing the per-pixel difference between the spectral erosion and dilation with a given structuring kernel and distance metric.

See: Plaza, Antonio, et al. 'Spatial/spectral endmember extraction by multidimensional morphological operations.' IEEE transactions on geoscience and remote sensing 40.9 (2002): 2025-2041.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: metric
args.description: The spectral distance metric to use. One of 'sam' (spectral angle mapper), 'sid' (spectral information divergence), 'sed' (squared Euclidean distance), or 'emd' (earth movers distance).

args.name: kernel
args.description: Connectedness kernel. Defaults to a square of radius 1 (8-way connected).

args.name: useCentroid
args.description: If true, distances are computed from the mean of all pixels under the kernel instead of the kernel's center pixel.

Image.spectralDilation.description:
Computes the spectral/spatial dilation of an image by computing the spectral distance of each pixel under a structuring kernel from the centroid of all pixels under the kernel and taking the most distant result.

See 'Spatial/spectral endmember extraction by multidimensional morphological operations.' IEEE transactions on geoscience and remote sensing 40.9 (2002): 2025-2041.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: metric
args.description: The spectral distance metric to use. One of 'sam' (spectral angle mapper), 'sid' (spectral information divergence), 'sed' (squared Euclidean distance), or 'emd' (earth movers distance).

args.name: kernel
args.description: Connectedness kernel. Defaults to a square of radius 1 (8-way connected).

args.name: useCentroid
args.description: If true, distances are computed from the mean of all pixels under the kernel instead of the kernel's center pixel.

Image.spectralDistance.description: Computes the per-pixel spectral distance between two images. If the images are array based then only the first band of each image is used; otherwise all bands are involved in the distance computation. The two images are therefore expected to contain the same number of bands or have the same 1-dimensional array length.

args.name: image1
args.description: The first image.

args.name: image2
args.description: The second image.

args.name: metric
args.description: The spectral distance metric to use. One of 'sam' (spectral angle mapper), 'sid' (spectral information divergence), 'sed' (squared Euclidean distance), or 'emd' (earth movers distance).

Image.reduceConnectedComponents.description: Applies a reducer to all of the pixels inside of each 'object'. Pixels are considered to belong to an object if they are connected (8-way) and have the same value in the 'label' band. The label band is only used to identify the connectedness; the rest are provided as inputs to the reducer.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply to pixels within the connected component.

args.name: labelBand
args.description: The name of the band to use to detect connectedness. If unspecified, the first band is used.

args.name: maxSize
args.description: Size of the neighborhood to consider when aggregating values. Any objects larger than maxSize in either the horizontal or vertical dimension will be masked, since portions of the object might be outside of the neighborhood.

Image.Segmentation.GMeans.description:
Performs G-Means clustering on the input image. Iteratively applies k-means followed by a normality test to automatically determine the number of clusters to use. The output contains a 'clusters' band containing the integer ID of the cluster that each pixel belongs to.

The algorithm can work either on a fixed grid of non-overlapping cells (gridSize, which can be smaller than a tile) or on tiles with overlap (neighborhoodSize). The default is to use tiles with no overlap. Clusters in one cell or tile are unrelated to clusters in another. Any cluster that spans a cell or tile boundary may receive two different labels in the two halves. Any input pixels with partial masks are fully masked in the output. This algorithm is only expected to perform well for images with a narrow dynamic range (i.e., bytes or shorts).

See: G. Hamerly and C. Elkan. 'Learning the k in k-means'. NIPS, 2003.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image for clustering.

args.name: numIterations
args.description: Number of iterations. Default 10.

args.name: pValue
args.description: Significance level for normality test.

args.name: neighborhoodSize
args.description: Neighborhood size. The amount to extend each tile (overlap) when computing the clusters. This option is mutually exclusive with gridSize.

args.name: gridSize
args.description: Grid cell-size. If greater than 0, kMeans will be run independently on cells of this size. This has the effect of limiting the size of any cluster to be gridSize or smaller. This option is mutually exclusive with neighborhoodSize.

args.name: uniqueLabels
args.description: If true, clusters are assigned unique IDs. Otherwise, they repeat per tile or grid cell.

Image.Segmentation.KMeans.description:
Performs K-Means clustering on the input image. Outputs a 1-band image containing the ID of the cluster that each pixel belongs to. The algorithm can work either on a fixed grid of non-overlapping cells (gridSize, which can be smaller than a tile) or on tiles with overlap (neighborhoodSize). The default is to use tiles with no overlap.

Clusters in one cell or tile are unrelated to clusters in another. Any cluster that spans a cell or tile boundary may receive two different labels in the two halves. Any input pixels with partial masks are fully masked in the output.

args.name: image
args.description: The input image for clustering.

args.name: numClusters
args.description: Number of clusters.

args.name: numIterations
args.description: Number of iterations.

args.name: neighborhoodSize
args.description: Neighborhood size. The amount to extend each tile (overlap) when computing the clusters. This option is mutually exclusive with gridSize.

args.name: gridSize
args.description: Grid cell-size. If greater than 0, kMeans will be run independently on cells of this size. This has the effect of limiting the size of any cluster to be gridSize or smaller. This option is mutually exclusive with neighborhoodSize.

args.name: forceConvergence
args.description: If true, an error is thrown if convergence is not achieved before numIterations.

args.name: uniqueLabels
args.description: If true, clusters are assigned unique IDs. Otherwise, they repeat per tile or grid cell.

ImageCollection.load.description: Returns the image collection given its ID.

args.name: id
args.description: The asset ID of the image collection.

args.name: version
args.description: The version of the asset. -1 signifies the latest version.

ImageCollection.loadZarrV2Array.description: Loads a Zarr v2 array with 3 or more dimensions (i.e., 1 or more non-spatial dimensions) as an ImageCollection by slicing along a specified non-spatial axis. The array attributes (.zattrs) must contain the field '_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS', which is a list of the names of each dimension (e.g., ['time', 'y', 'x']). There must be at least two dimensions, with the final two representing Y and X respectively (e.g., ['lat', 'lon']). The supported compression codecs are 'blosc', 'gzip', 'lz4', 'zlib', and 'zstd'. The supported blosc meta-compression codecs are 'lz4', lz4hc', 'zlib', and 'zstd' ('blosclz' is not supported).

args.name: uri
args.description: The Cloud Storage URI of the .zarray file to load. A .zmetadata file must be present in the parent directory of the array's directory (e.g., for 'gs://b/o/.zarray', 'gs://b/.zmetadata' must be present). The bucket metadata must be accessible (requires the `storage.buckets.get` permission which is provided by the role "Storage Legacy Bucket Reader" among others, see https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam-roles) and the bucket must be located in the US multi-region, a dual-region including US-CENTRAL1, or the US-CENTRAL1 region.

args.name: proj
args.description: The projection of the array.

args.name: axis
args.description: The non-spatial axis (0-indexed) along which to slice the array to create an ImageCollection. Each image in the collection represents a single slice (length 1) along this axis. If null, defaults to 0. The value must be in the range [0, N-1], where N is the number of non-spatial dimensions (i.e., total dimensions - 2). The array must have at least one non-spatial dimension (i.e., be at least 3 dimensional).

args.name: starts
args.description: The indices (inclusive) at which to start taking slices along each non-spatial dimension. If null, slices will start at index 0 for all non-spatial dimensions. If specified, this list must have a length equal to the number of non-spatial dimensions (total dimensions - 2). An individual element within the list may be null, which defaults to 0 for that dimension. Negative indices are counted from the end of the dimension (e.g., -1 is the last element).

args.name: ends
args.description: The indices (exclusive) at which to stop taking slices along each non-spatial dimension. If null, slices will extend to the end of each corresponding non-spatial dimension (i.e., defaults to the length of the dimension). If specified, this list must have a length equal to the number of non-spatial dimensions (total dimensions - 2). An individual element within the list may be null, which also defaults to the length of that dimension. Negative indices are counted from the end of the dimension (e.g., -1 is the last element).

ImageCollection.cast.description: Casts some or all bands of each image in an ImageCollection to the specified types.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to cast.

args.name: bandTypes
args.description: A dictionary from band name to band types. Types can be PixelTypes or strings. The valid strings are: 'int8', 'int16', 'int32', 'int64', 'uint8', 'uint16', 'uint32', 'byte', 'short', 'int', 'long', 'float', and 'double'. Must include all bands already in any image in the collection. If this includes bands that are not already in an input image, they will be added to the image as transparent bands.

args.name: bandOrder
args.description: A list specifying the order of the bands in the result. Must match the keys of bandTypes.

ImageCollection.combine.description:
Makes a new collection that is a copy of the images in primary, adding all the bands from the image in secondary with a matching ID. If there are no matching IDs, the resulting collection will be empty. This is equivalent to an inner join on ID with merging of the bands of the result.

Note that this algorithm assumes that for a matching pair of inputs, both have the same footprint and metadata.

args.name: primary
args.description: The primary collection to join.

args.name: secondary
args.description: The secondary collection to join.

args.name: overwrite
args.description: If true, bands with the same name will get overwritten. If false, bands with the same name will be renamed.

ImageCollection.formaTrend.description:
Computes the long and short term trends of a time series or optionally, the trends of the ratio of the time series and a covariate. The long term trend is estimated from the linear term of a regression on the full time series. The short term trend is computed as the windowed minimum over the time series.

The time series and covariate series are expected to contain a single band each, and the time series is expected to be evenly spaced in time. The output is 4 float bands: the long and short term trends, the t-test of the long term trend against the time series, and the Bruce Hansen test of parameter stability.

args.name: timeSeries
args.description: Collection from which to extract trends.

args.name: covariates
args.description: Cofactors to use in the trend analysis.

args.name: windowSize
args.description: Short term trend analysis window size, in images.

ImageCollection.fromImages.description: Returns the image collection containing the given images.

args.name: images
args.description: The images to include in the collection.

ImageCollection.getRegion.description: Output an array of values for each [pixel, band, image] tuple in  an ImageCollection. The output contains rows of  id, lon, lat, time, and all bands for each image that intersects  each pixel in the given region. Attempting to extract more than 1048576  values will result in an error.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to extract data from.

args.name: geometry
args.description: The region over which to extract data.

args.name: scale
args.description: A nominal scale in meters of the projection to work in.

args.name: crs
args.description: The projection to work in. If unspecified, defaults to EPSG:4326. If specified in addition to scale, the projection is rescaled to the specified scale.

args.name: crsTransform
args.description: The array of CRS transform values. This is a row-major ordering of a 3x2 affine transform. This option is mutually exclusive with the scale option, and will replace any transform already set on the given projection.

ImageCollection.reduce.description:
Applies a reducer across all of the images in a collection.
If the reducer has a single input, it will be applied separately to each band of the collection; otherwise it must have the same number of inputs as the collection has bands.
The reducer output names determine the names of the output bands: reducers with multiple inputs will use the output names directly, while reducers with a single input will prefix the output name with the input band name (e.g., '10_mean', '20_mean').

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply to the given collection.

args.name: parallelScale
args.description: A scaling factor used to limit memory use; using a larger parallelScale (e.g., 2 or 4) may enable computations that run out of memory with the default.

ImageCollection.merge.description: Merges two image collections into one. The result has all the images that were in either collection.

args.name: collection1
args.description: The first collection to merge.

args.name: collection2
args.description: The second collection to merge.

ImageCollection.mosaic.description: Composites all the images in a collection, using the mask.

args.name: collection
args.description: The collection to mosaic.

ImageCollection.qualityMosaic.description: Composites all the images in a collection, using a quality band as a per-pixel ordering function.

args.name: collection
args.description: The collection to mosaic.

args.name: qualityBand
args.description: The name of the quality band in the collection.

ImageCollection.toBands.description:
Converts a collection to a single multi-band image containing all of the bands of every image in the collection. Output bands are named by prefixing the existing band names with the image id from which it came (e.g., 'image1_band1').

Note: The maximum number of bands is 5000.

args.name: collection
args.description: The input collection.

reduce.min.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the minimum value of each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.max.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the maximum value of each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.count.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the number of images with a valid mask at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.sum.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the sum of all values at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.product.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the product of all values at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.mean.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the mean of all values at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.and.description: Reduces an image collection by setting each pixel to 1 if and only if all the non-masked values at that pixel are non-zero across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.or.description: Reduces an image collection by setting each pixel to 1 if and only if any of the non-masked values at that pixel are non-zero across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.median.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the median of all values at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

reduce.mode.description: Reduces an image collection by calculating the most common value at each pixel across the stack of all matching bands. Bands are matched by name.

args.name: collection
args.description: The image collection to reduce.

List.add.description: Appends the element to the end of list.

List.cat.description: Concatenates the contents of other onto list.

List.contains.description: Returns true if list contains element.

List.containsAll.description: Returns true if list contains all of the elements of other, regardless of order.

List.distinct.description: Returns a copy of list without duplicate elements.

List.equals.description: Returns true if list contains the same elements as other, in the same order.

List.filter.description: Filters a list to only the elements that match the given filter. To filter list items that aren't images or features, test a property named 'item', e.g., ee.Filter.gt('item', 3).

List.flatten.description: Flattens any sublists into a single list.

List.frequency.description: Returns the number of elements in list equal to element.

List.get.description: Returns the element at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list.

List.getArray.description: Returns the array at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list. If the value is not a array, an error will occur.

List.getGeometry.description: Returns the geometry at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list. If the value is not a geometry, an error will occur.

List.getNumber.description: Returns the number at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list. If the value is not a number, an error will occur.

List.getString.description: Returns the string at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list. If the value is not a string, an error will occur.

List.indexOf.description: Returns the position of the first occurrence of element in list, or -1 if list does not contain element.

List.indexOfSublist.description: Returns the starting position of the first occurrence of target within list, or -1 if there is no such occurrence.

List.insert.description: Inserts element at the specified position in list. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list.

List.iterate.description: Iterate an algorithm over a list. The algorithm is expected to take two objects, the current list item, and the result from the previous iteration or the value of first for the first iteration.

List.join.description:
Returns a string containing the elements of the list joined together with the specified separator between elements.

Note: The string form of list elements which are not strings, numbers, or booleans is currently not well-defined and subject to change.

List.lastIndexOfSubList.description: Returns the starting position of the last occurrence of target within list, or -1 if there is no such occurrence.

List.length.description: Returns the number of elements in list.

List.map.description: Map an algorithm over a list. The algorithm is expected to take an Object and return an Object.

args.name: dropNulls
args.description: If true, the mapped algorithm is allowed to return nulls, and the elements for which it returns nulls will be dropped.

List.reduce.description: Apply a reducer to a list. If the reducer takes more than 1 input, then each element in the list is assumed to be a list of inputs. If the reducer returns a single output, it is returned directly, otherwise returns a dictionary containing the named reducer outputs.

List.remove.description: Removes the first occurrence of the specified element from list, if it is present.

List.removeAll.description: Removes from list all of the elements that are contained in other list.

List.repeat.description: Returns a new list containing value repeated count times.

args.name: value
args.description: The value to repeat.

args.name: count
args.description: The number of times to repeat.

List.replace.description: Replaces the first occurrence of oldval in list with newval.

List.replaceAll.description: Replaces all occurrences of oldval in list with newval.

List.reverse.description: Reverses the order of the elements in list.

List.rotate.description: Rotates the elements of the list by the specified distance.

List.sequence.description: Generate a sequence of numbers from start to end (inclusive) in increments of step, or in count equally-spaced increments. If end is not specified it is computed from start + step * count, so at least one of end or count must be specified.

args.name: start
args.description: The starting number.

args.name: end
args.description: The ending number.

args.name: step
args.description: The increment.

args.name: count
args.description: The number of increments.

List.set.description: Replaces the value at the specified position in list with element. A negative index counts backwards from the end of the list.

List.shuffle.description: Randomly permute the specified list. Note that the permutation order will always be the same for any given seed, unless the value for seed is 'false'.

args.name: seed
args.description: A long integer to use as a seed for the randomization. If the boolean value of 'false' is passed, then a completely random and unreproducible order will be generated.

List.size.description: Returns the number of elements in list.

List.slice.description: Returns a portion of list between the start index, inclusive, and end index, exclusive. Negative values for start or end count backwards from the end of the list. Values greater than the size of the list are legal but are truncated to the size of list.

List.sort.description: Sorts the list into ascending order. If the 'keys' argument is provided, then it is sorted first, and the elements of 'list' are placed in the same order.

args.name: list
args.description: The list to sort.

args.name: keys
args.description: Optional keys to sort by. If 'keys' is provided, it must have the same length as 'list'.

List.splice.description: Starting at the start index, removes count elements from list and insert the contents of other at that location. If start is negative, it counts backwards from the end of the list.

List.swap.description: Swaps the elements at the specified positions. A negative position counts backwards from the end of the list.

List.unzip.description: Transposes a list of lists, extracting the first element of each inner list into one list the second elements into another, etc., up to the length of the shortest inner list. The remaining items are discarded. The result is a list of lists.

List.zip.description: Pairs the elements of two lists to create a list of two-element lists. When the input lists are of different sizes, the final list has the same size as the shortest one.

args.name: input
args.description: An object to convert to a dictionary. Either a JSON dictionary or a list of alternating key/value pairs. Keys must be strings.

Dictionary.combine.description: Combines two dictionaries. In the case of duplicate names, the output will contain the value of the second dictionary unless overwrite is false. Null values in both dictionaries are ignored / removed.

Dictionary.contains.description: Returns true if the dictionary contains the given key.

Dictionary.fromLists.description: Construct a dictionary from two parallel lists of keys and values.

args.name: keys
args.description: A list of keys.

args.name: values
args.description: A list of values.

Dictionary.get.description: Extracts a named value from a dictionary. If the dictionary does not contain the given key, then defaultValue is returned, unless it is null.

Dictionary.getArray.description: Extracts a named array value from a dictionary.

Dictionary.getGeometry.description: Extracts a named geometry value from a dictionary.

Dictionary.getNumber.description: Extracts a named number value from a dictionary.

Dictionary.getString.description: Extracts a named string value from a dictionary.

Dictionary.keys.description: Retrieve the keys of a dictionary as a list. The keys will be sorted in natural order.

Dictionary.map.description: Map an algorithm over a dictionary. The algorithm is expected to take 2 arguments, a key from the existing dictionary and the value it corresponds to, and return a new value for the given key. If the algorithm returns null, the key is dropped.

Dictionary.remove.description: Returns a dictionary with the specified keys removed.

args.name: selectors
args.description: A list of keys names or regular expressions of key names to remove.

args.name: ignoreMissing
args.description: Ignore selectors that don't match at least 1 key.

args.name: from
args.description: A list of keys to be renamed.

args.name: to
args.description: A list of the new names for the keys listed in the 'from' parameter. Must have the same length as the 'from' list.

args.name: overwrite
args.description: Allow overwriting existing properties with the same name.

Dictionary.select.description: Returns a dictionary with only the specified keys.

args.name: selectors
args.description: A list of keys or regular expressions to select.

args.name: ignoreMissing
args.description: Ignore selectors that don't match at least 1 key.

Dictionary.set.description: Set a value in a dictionary.

Dictionary.size.description: Returns the number of entries in a dictionary.

Dictionary.toArray.description: Returns numeric values of a dictionary as an array. If no keys are specified, all values are returned in the natural ordering of the dictionary's keys. The default 'axis' is 0.

Dictionary.values.description: Returns the values of a dictionary as a list. If no keys are specified, all values are returned in the natural ordering of the dictionary's keys.

Dictionary.toImage.description: Creates an image of constants from values in a dictionary. The bands of the image are ordered and named according to the names argument. If no names are specified, the bands are sorted alpha-numerically.

args.name: dictionary
args.description: The dictionary to convert.

args.name: names
args.description: The order of the output bands.

args.name: string1
args.description: The first string.

args.name: string2
args.description: The second string.

String.compareTo.description: Compares two strings lexicographically. Returns: the value 0 if the two strings are lexicographically equal; -1 if string1 is less than string2; and 1 if string1 is lexicographically greater than string2.

args.name: string1
args.description: The string to compare.

args.name: string2
args.description: The string to be compared.

args.name: string
args.description: The string to decode.

String.encodeJSON.description: Encodes an object to JSON. Supports primitives, lists, and dictionaries.

args.name: object
args.description: The object to encode.

String.equals.description: Checks for string equality with a given object. Returns true if the target is a string and is lexicographically equal to the reference, or false otherwise.

args.name: reference
args.description: The string to compare for equality.

args.name: target
args.description: The second object to check for equality.

String.index.description: Searches a string for the first occurrence of a substring.  Returns the index of the first match, or -1.

args.name: target
args.description: The string to search.

args.name: pattern
args.description: The string to find.

String.length.description: Returns the length of a string.

args.name: string
args.description: The string from which to get the length.

String.match.description: Matches a string against a regular expression. Returns a list of matching strings.

args.name: input
args.description: The string in which to search.

args.name: regex
args.description: The regular expression to match.

args.name: flags
args.description: A string specifying a combination of regular expression flags, specifically one or more of: 'g' (global match) or 'i' (ignore case).

String.replace.description: Returns a new string with some or all matches of a pattern replaced.

args.name: input
args.description: The string in which to search.

args.name: regex
args.description: The regular expression to match.

args.name: replacement
args.description: The string that replaces the matched substring.

A printf-style format string. For example, '%.2f' produces numbers formatted like '3.14', and '%05d' produces numbers formatted like '00042'. The format string must satisfy the following criteria:
  1. Zero or more prefix characters.
  2. Exactly one '%'.
  3. Zero or more modifier characters in the set [#-+ 0,(.\d].
  4. Exactly one conversion character in the set [sdoxXeEfgGaA].
  5. Zero or more suffix characters.
For more about format strings, see https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Formatter.html

Image.arraySlice.description:
Creates a subarray by slicing out each position along the given axis from the 'start' (inclusive) to 'end' (exclusive) by increments of 'step'.

The result will have as many dimensions as the input, and the same length in all directions except the slicing axis, where the length will be the number of positions from 'start' to 'end' by 'step' that are in range of the input array's length along 'axis'. This means the result can be length 0 along the given axis if start=end, or if the start or end values are entirely out of range.

args.name: input
args.description: Input array image.

args.name: axis
args.description: Axis to subset.

args.name: start
args.description: The coordinate of the first slice (inclusive) along 'axis'. Negative numbers are used to position the start of slicing relative to the end of the array, where -1 starts at the last position on the axis, -2 starts at the next to last position, etc. There must one band for start indices, or one band per 'input' band. If this argument is not set or masked at some pixel, then the slice at that pixel will start at index 0.

args.name: end
args.description: The coordinate (exclusive) at which to stop taking slices. By default this will be the length of the given axis. The bands of each image are laid  out along the second axis of the array, in the order the bands  appear in that image. The array element type will be the union of  the types of each band.

args.description: Images to concatenate. A separate concatenation is done per band, so all the images must have the same dimensionality and shape per band, except length along the concatenation axis.

args.name: axis
args.description: Axis to concatenate along; must be at least 0 and at most the minimum dimension of any band in the collection.

args.name: dropMasked
args.description:
If false (the default), the mask value of the output pixel is the minimum of the masks of the input pixels. If any image in the collection within the computation bounding box is completely masked at a pixel, that output pixel will be masked. As a result, every unmasked output pixel array will have the same size.
If true, the mask value of the output pixel is the maximum of the mask of the inputs. Completely masked images at that pixel are ignored and do not contribute data to the output array. The output arrays will therefore not necessarily have the same size for each pixel.

Array.reduce.description:
Apply a reducer to an array by collapsing all the input values along each specified axis into a single output value computed by the reducer.

The output always has the same dimensionality as the input, and the individual axes are affected as follows:

  • The axes specified in the 'axes' parameter have their length reduced to 1 (by applying the reducer).
  • If the reducer has multiple inputs or multiple outputs, the axis specified in 'fieldAxis' will be used to provide the reducer's inputs and store the reducer's outputs.
  • All other axes are unaffected (independent reductions are performed).

args.name: array
args.description: The array.

args.name: reducer
args.description: The reducer to apply. Each of its outputs must be a number, not an array or other type.

args.name: axes
args.description: The list of axes over which to reduce. The output will have a length of 1 in all these axes.

args.name: fieldAxis
args.description: The axis to use as the reducer's input and output fields. Only required if the reducer has multiple inputs or multiple outputs, in which case the axis must have length equal to the number of reducer inputs, and in the result it will have length equal to the number of reducer outputs.

The result will have as many dimensions as the input, and the same length in all directions except the slicing axis, where the length will be the number of positions from 'start' to 'end' by 'step' that are in range of the input array's length along 'axis'. This means the result can be length 0 along the given axis if start=end, or if the start or end values are entirely out of range.

Array.eigen.description:
Computes the real eigenvectors and eigenvalues of a square 2D array of A rows and A columns. Returns an array with A rows and A+1 columns, where each row contains an eigenvalue in the first column, and the corresponding eigenvector in the remaining A columns. The rows are sorted by eigenvalue, in descending order.

This implementation uses DecompositionFactory.eig() from https://ejml.org.

args.description: A square, 2D array from which to compute the eigenvalue decomposition.

Image.matrixMultiply.description: Returns the matrix multiplication A * B for each matched pair of bands in image1 and image2. If either image1 or image2 has only 1 band, then it is used against all the bands in the other image. If the images have the same number of bands, but not the same names, they're used pairwise in the natural order. The output bands are named for the longer of the two inputs, or if they're equal in length, in image1's order. The type of the output pixels is the union of the input types.

Image.matrixSolve.description: Solves for x in the matrix equation A * x = B, finding a least-squares solution if A is overdetermined for each matched pair of bands in image1 and image2. If either image1 or image2 has only 1 band, then it is used against all the bands in the other image. If the images have the same number of bands, but not the same names, they're used pairwise in the natural order. The output bands are named for the longer of the two inputs, or if they're equal in length, in image1's order. The type of the output pixels is the union of the input types.

Model.fromAiPlatformPredictor.description: Returns an ee.Model from a description of an AI Platform prediction model. (See https://cloud.google.com/ml-engine/).

args.name: projectName
args.description: The Google Cloud project that owns the model. Deprecated: use "projectId" instead.

args.name: projectId
args.description: The ID of the Google Cloud project that owns the model.

args.name: modelName
args.description: The name of the model.

args.name: version
args.description: The model version. Defaults to the AI Platform default model version.

args.name: region
args.description: The model deployment region. Defaults to "us-central1".

args.name: inputProperties
args.description: Properties passed with each prediction instance. Image predictions are tiled, so these properties will be replicated into each image tile instance. Defaults to no properties.

args.name: inputTypeOverride
args.description: Types to which model inputs will be coerced if specified. Both Image bands and Image/Feature properties are valid.

args.name: inputShapes
args.description: The fixed shape of input array bands. For each array band not specified, the fixed array shape will be automatically deduced from a non-masked pixel.

args.name: proj
args.description: The input projection at which to sample all bands. Defaults to the default projection of an image's first band.

args.name: fixInputProj
args.description: If true, pixels will be sampled in a fixed projection specified by 'proj'. The output projection is used otherwise. Defaults to false.

args.name: inputTileSize
args.description: Rectangular dimensions of pixel tiles passed in to prediction instances. Required for image predictions.

args.name: inputOverlapSize
args.description: Amount of adjacent-tile overlap in X/Y along each edge of pixel tiles passed in to prediction instances. Defaults to [0, 0].

args.name: outputTileSize
args.description: Rectangular dimensions of pixel tiles returned from AI Platform. Defaults to the value in 'inputTileSize'.

args.name: outputBands
args.description: A map from output band names to a dictionary of output band info. Valid band info fields are 'type' and 'dimensions'. 'type' should be a ee.PixelType describing the output band, and 'dimensions' is an optional integer with the number of dimensions in that band e.g., "outputBands: {'p': {'type': ee.PixelType.int8(), 'dimensions': 1}}". Required for image predictions.

args.name: outputProperties
args.description: A map from output property names to a dictionary of output property info. Valid property info fields are 'type' and 'dimensions'. 'type' should be a ee.PixelType describing the output property, and 'dimensions' is an optional integer with the number of dimensions for that property if it is an array e.g., "outputBands: {'p': {'type': ee.PixelType.int8(), 'dimensions': 1}}". Required for predictions from FeatureCollections.

args.name: outputMultiplier
args.description: An approximation to the increase in data volume for the model outputs over the model inputs. If specified this must be >= 1. This is only needed if the model produces more data than it consumes, e.g., a model that takes 5 bands and produces 10 outputs per pixel.
